# QS-CFW-1931-62 - Quality specification - gear blank CFW-1931-62 (8620)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-1931-62

Scope
- This quality specification applies to the manufacture, inspection, and disposition of gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62), material designation 8620, produced at Plant P3.  
- The specification defines acceptance criteria for metallurgical hardness, bore geometry, and maximum forging mass, and establishes required inspection methods, documentation, and nonconformance handling for production and incoming inspection.  
- Background: CFW-1931-62 gear blanks are intermediate forgings destined for downstream machining and heat treatment. Consistent hardness and dimensional control of the bore are critical to achieve predictable gear performance after finishing and heat treatment. The limits in this document reflect forged state acceptance intended to ensure process stability and minimize rework downstream.

Requirements table
- Part: CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62)  
- Hardness: The hardness range for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 38-41 HRC. This applies to measured locations on the finished forging surface where machining stock is intended to be removed or where specified by order. Hardness outside this range is a nonconformance subject to disposition.  
- Bore diameter tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is ±0.08 mm. Inspectable features include the finished bore prior to any final machining operations. Bore runout, concentricity, and surface condition are assessed during inspection; the dimensional tolerance above governs acceptance.  
- Maximum forging mass: The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 97.9 kg. Any forging claimed to exceed this mass at time of final forging inspection shall be segregated and dispositioned per the nonconformance handling section.

Inspection method
- Purpose: Define how to verify each requirement in the requirements table and the records to be retained. Methods are selected to be practical for shop floor verification while providing defensible measurement data for quality records. Rationale: Direct measurement and standardized hardness testing give rapid confirmation of process output and allow timely corrective action if trends indicate drift. Examples given are illustrative of typical checks and recording practice.  
- Hardness measurement: Conduct hardness checks on representative locations on each forging surface intended for subsequent machining or where specified by the purchase order. Use a calibrated Rockwell tester capable of reporting HRC. Perform verification by experienced personnel following instrument manufacturer recommendations for indenter selection and surface preparation. Record each measured value and identify the piece serial or heat reference in the inspection record. Acceptance criterion: hardness must fall within the hardness range for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 38-41 HRC. Example: For a production lot, record the sequence of sample measurements, annotate any outliers, and include a photograph of the test indication when surface finish is marginal.  
- Bore diameter measurement: Measure the bore using an appropriate internal diameter measuring device that provides traceable calibration. Verify at multiple axial positions and record the measurement locations. Acceptance criterion: measurement results must conform to the bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is ±0.08 mm relative to the nominal bore specified on the manufacturing print. Example: Document a set of measurements from near each end of the bore and mid span, noting any taper or irregularity. Any single measurement outside of tolerance requires the part to be segregated and forwarded for engineering disposition.  
- Mass verification: Verify forging mass using a calibrated scale at final forging inspection. Acceptance criterion: the maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 97.9 kg. When reported mass equals the maximum forging mass for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 97.9 kg, confirm calculations and ensure packing and tagging accurately reflect measured value. If mass exceeds the maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 97.9 kg, follow nonconformance handling.  
- Records to keep: Maintain an inspection pack for each lot that includes hardness readings with location map, raw bore measurement data with measurement device ID, mass verification printout, inspector signature, and the process route for the heat/lot. Retain records in the document control system and attach to the batch record used for downstream operations. Records support root cause analysis and are required for any disposition decision.

Nonconformance handling
- Segregation: Any forging found outside the stated acceptance criteria shall be segregated from conforming inventory and clearly tagged with a nonconformance identifier. Bring the piece to the attention of the quality supervisor for immediate evaluation.  
- Evaluation and disposition: Quality shall perform an evaluation that includes review of inspection records, process data, and potential impact on downstream operations. Where an out-of-tolerance condition affects only a removable region or can be corrected without compromising integrity, an engineering disposition may allow rework. Where the condition could affect performance after final processing, the forging must be rejected or reprocessed under engineering authorization. Rationale: Objective evaluation limits unnecessary scrap while protecting product function. Example: a bore out of tolerance that can be corrected by final machining within the allowed tolerance band at the next operation may be accepted under controlled rework instructions; any such acceptance must be recorded.  
- Root cause and corrective action: For each nonconformance, document root cause findings and corrective actions taken, including changes to tooling, process parameters, or inspection frequency. Record verification of corrective action effectiveness in subsequent inspection records.  
- Disposition records: All disposition decisions, approvals, and confirmations of corrective action must be recorded and stored with the inspection records for the lot. These records are the basis for trending and continuous improvement and must be available for internal review.

End of document
